The Battle of Lesser Zelenchuk was a military engagement fought in September 1836 during the Russo-Circassian War between forces of the Russian Empire and Circassian warriors under the command of Ale Khirtsizhiqo, a prominent Abzakh leader. Initially planning to raid Batalpashinskaya, Circassians diverted their attack to a Russian post near Kislovodsk after their plan was uncovered by Russian intelligence.
History
In September 1836, around 2,000 Circassians—primarily Abzakhs, joined by Shapsugs and Hajjret Kabardians—gathered under Ale Khirtsizhiqo and his son to raid Russian positions. About 1,200 had taken a blood oath
After Russian General Zass learned of the plan, the Circassians changed their route and attacked a Russian post near Kislovodsk, taking captives and loot. Russian troops, aided by loyalist Circassians and Nogais, ambushed them near the Lesser Zelenchuk River.
A battle followed. Russian artillery and snipers dominated early stages. Ale reached sniper positions, killed several, but was fatally shot. He tried to destroy his weapons before dying. His son and the son's atalık also died.
Circassians recovered his body under fire, killed their horses to prevent capture, and buried 41 fallen, including Ale, on a hilltop.
